paragraphs: Craft Education sells software for running registered apprenticeships and work-based learning programs. The platform, called Craft Connect, is built for employers, education partners, and intermediaries. Healthcare and education are the fields it is designed around first, though the company says the platform itself is field-agnostic.

A program administrator configures the program to registered-apprenticeship standards and invites learners, employers, and evaluators. Learners then log on-the-job hours against the work-process schedule from any browser. Mentors and reviewers work a queue rather than an inbox, approving hours, submissions, and competencies or sending them back, with every action time-stamped. Sign-offs roll into competency records, and one data model produces the WIOA, Perkins, RAPIDS, and Workforce Pell exports funders and accreditors accept.

The company describes itself as an essential part of WGU and puts mission before margin. Its stated purpose is to change lives for the better by creating pathways to opportunity. For buyers in IT, security, and procurement, the company states SOC2 compliance, invitation-gated access, and audit-ready records by default. It also cites WCAG 2.2 accessibility with a VPAT available and reporting to USDOL and RAPIDS.

quote.text: Craft Connect is not trying to replace the systems you already run.
